name: Echopraxist
special: Peculiar extradimensional visitors, attempting to understand the world they have entered by mimicking its inhabitants. In their 'true' form Echopraxists resemble iridescent fog, but they are able to take the shape of any living creature that catches their attention.

Living Echo: When encountered, each Echopraxist choses one PC to perfectly mimic. They take on the appearance of the PC, as well as their Level, current HP, AV, and all other weapons and equipment. Damaging an Echopraxist causes equal damage to the PC they are echoing.

attacks.name: Entropic Touch

special: Cursed revenants, the remains of those who thought to master entropy and instead became her servants. All things wither at their touch, ageing centuries beneath the Wight's sour grasp.

Entropic Touch: targets struck by the Wight lose d3 maximum HP, and lose d3 points of AV. Hit Points lost in this way are never regained, nor can armour eroded by the Wight be repaired. Melee weapons which strike the Wight lose one dice size of damage permanently.

resistances.notes: No damage resistance/immunity printed in stat block. (Entropic Touch is an attack effect, not a defensive resistance.)

combat_note: Entropic Touch permanently reduces target max HP and AV; melee weapons striking the Wight permanently lose one die size of damage.

Nonviolent: Exemplars will only strike in self-defence, after repeated attempts to negotiate.
Beauty is Terror: all PCs lose 1 point of EGO for each combat round spent in an unveiled Exemplar's presence. This loss is doubled if the Exemplar is modelled after their own species.
combat_note: Perfect Strike always hits for d20. Beauty is Terror drains EGO each round in presence (doubled vs same species). Nonviolent unless self-defence.

Disguise: Face Dancers can replicate the face and body of any adult true-kin within hours of studying them. Cacogen and newbeasts are more challenging, although a passable mimicry can be achieved using prosthetics.
Malleable: the Dancer's skeleton is highly flexible. They take half damage from bludgeoning attacks, and can fit through any gap wider than their skull.

resistances.notes: Malleable: takes half damage from bludgeoning attacks.

name: Faa Sniper
special: The Faa are adept at ranged combat, training from childhood with their firearms. Those who show abnormal talent are inducted into the use of the sniper rifle, acting as support for Faa raids.

Headshot: at the start of each combat round, before initative is determined, the Sniper picks one foe in line of sight for elimination. If at the end of the combat round the Sniper still has line of sight on the target, they are shot and reduced to 0 HP, with no Save possible. If the PC targeted has negative HP, this attack is instantly fatal. Creatures without heads suffer d10 damage instead.
Hidden: Snipers blend into the environment and cannot be targeted if they do not move. When they fire, the target can make an INT Save to pinpoint their locaton.

name: Fleshwarp
special: A cacogenic abhuman, consisting of an atrophied, vestigal torso and a multitude of questing limbs. Fleshwarps are blessed with rapid cellular regeneration, and can heal even mortal wounds within minutes. As they grow, more and more biomass is extruded into their limbs, creating skittering spiderlike abominations.
Limbs: the Fleshwarp has a number of limbs equal to its Level (2d6).
Regeneration: a Fleshwarp regenerates HP equal to its Level at the start of each round. Damage caused by fire or acid ignores this.

Graft: If the target fails an opposed STR save, the Fleshwarp attaches one of its limbs to the victim's torso. The Fleshwarp's Level and number of limbs are lowered by -1 (if this would reduce the Level below 1, the Fleshwarp dies). The victim fills an item slot with a Wound: Grafted Arm. The Grafted Arm is LVL1 and has the AV of its host. It makes an unarmed attack each round (d4) targeted at any one near its host. Damage dealt to the Grafted Arm is shared between the host and the limb.

resistances.notes: Regeneration (HP = Level/round) is negated by fire and acid damage — these bypass its healing, but no formal resistance/immunity to a damage type is stated.

combat_note: LVL printed as '2d6*' (variable, asterisk-noted); HP not given. Limbs = Level. Regenerates HP = Level/round, but fire and acid ignore (bypass) the regeneration.

special: An incursion from another fevered sphere of reality, a bizarre hypergeometric monster whose mere regard unwinds the warp and weft of space-time.

Recursive Gaze: Any PC fixed with the Recursive Gaze must repeat the action they took the turn before, with no save allowed. This effect is broken if the Fractalisk's gaze is interrupted, or if the creature dies.
Self Similar: Wounding a Fractalisk without the use of hypergeometric weaponry or anti-paradoxical normality gas causes the creature to spit into two identical Fractalisks.
